senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to swing, be light, move to and fro; v. שׁוֹט II,] to roam, fly, float, swim.
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 14a:12">M. Kat. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>לָשׁוּט</he> if he goes abroad to roam (for mere pleasure), opp. <he>למזונות</he> for support, <he>להרויחא</he> for profit in business.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 15b:12">B. Bath. 15ᵇ</cite> (Satan says) <he>שַׁטְתִּי בכל וכ׳</he> I roamed all over the world, but have found none so faithful as &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 5:2">Bets. V, 2</cite> (<cite ref="Beitzah 36b:9">36ᵇ</cite>) <he>לא שָׁטִין על פני המים</he> you must not float on the water (swim on the Sabbath).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 6:2:3">Y. Shek. VI, 50ᵃ</cite> top (ref. to <cite ref="Ezekiel 47:5">Ez. XLVII, 5</cite>) <he>כי גאו המים מי שחו מִלָּשׁוּט</he> (omit <he>מהו מי שחו</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l., p. 55) the waters were risen … too high for swimming; a. e.—[Y. B. Mets. VIII, end, 11ᵈ <he>בששטן</he>, read: <he>בששטפן</he>, v. <cite ref="U00762"><he>שָׁטַף</he></cite>.]
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 101:2">Yalk. Gen. 101</cite> <he>עד שהיתה קומתו מְשׁוֹטֶטֶת בדמעות</he> until his body swam in tears.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 30b:12">Kidd. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>אף לַהֲשִׁיטוֹ בנהר</he> a father is also bound to have his son taught swimming; <cite ref="Tosefta Kiddushin 1:11">Tosef. ib. I, 11</cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 9:9:1">Koh. R. to IX, 9</cite> <he>להושיטו</he> (corr. acc.).
